12 A shelf XY is 0.40 m long and is attached to a wall at end X.
It is kept horizontal by a wire attached to Y and to the wall, as shown.
wire
15 N
wall
shelf
30
Y
X
0.40 m
The tension force in the wire is 15 N at an angle of 30 to the horizontal.
What is the moment of this force about point X?
A
3.0 N m
B
5.2 N m
C
6.9 N m
D
12 N m

hints: Notice the $15 \text{ N}$ tension acts at Y, which is $0.40 \text{ m}$ horizontally from the pivot X.
Only the component of the tension perpendicular to the horizontal shelf contributes to the moment about X, so focus on the $30^{\circ}$ angle to the horizontal.
Work out $15 \sin 30^{\circ}$ to get the vertical pull at Y in $\text{N}$, then multiply by $0.40 \text{ m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the pivot and distance: the force is applied at Y, with position vector of magnitude $0.40 \text{ m}$ from X along the horizontal shelf.
State the rule: moment about X is $\text{force} \times \text{perpendicular distance}$, or $rF\sin\theta$ where $\theta$ is the angle between $r$ and $F$.
Resolve the $15 \text{ N}$ tension at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal: vertical component $= 15\sin 30^{\circ} = 15 \times 0.5 = 7.5 \text{ N}$ upward.
The horizontal component $15\cos 30^{\circ}$ acts along the line of the shelf level through Y, so its perpendicular distance from X is zero and its moment is zero.
Calculate the moment from the vertical component: $M = 7.5 \text{ N} \times 0.40 \text{ m} = 3.0 \text{ N m}$ anticlockwise.
Unit check gives $\text{N m}$ with sensible precision to two significant figures. This is option A

A.explanation: Moment is $0.40 \times 15 \sin 30^{\circ} = 3.0 \text{ N m}$, the vertical component times the horizontal distance from X.

B.explanation: This uses $15\cos 30^{\circ} \times 0.40$, the horizontal component which acts parallel to the shelf and has no moment about X.

C.explanation: This is larger than $15 \times 0.40$ can give with a $30^{\circ}$ component, so it cannot be the resolved moment.

D.explanation: This ignores the $30^{\circ}$ angle and doubles the distance, whereas only the perpendicular component $15\sin 30^{\circ}$ contributes.
